items.title: Work with the Figma agent in Dev Mode
items.excerpt: Figma release notes (New release, Dev Mode / AI): developers can now use the Figma agent inside Dev Mode to inspect and understand designs, compare versions, ask for code snippets and get bulk asset download links.

items.title: Gestalt beat Claude Fable 5.2 in 78% of blind design votes
items.excerpt: A stealth model called Gestalt took first place on Contra Labs and BenchFlow's Frontier Design Benchmark at 1,931 Elo, a 218-point lead; professional designers picked it over Claude Fable 5.2 in 78% of blind head-to-head votes. (Off-list: no on-list outlet covered it.)

items.title: Lovable keeps working while you answer its questions
items.excerpt: Lovable's agent can now ask a question and keep building whatever doesn't depend on the answer, picking an option for the rest and reworking it if you choose differently; it still waits before hard-to-undo steps such as deleting data.

items.title: Everyone knows sparkles mean AI. Use them to make design audits easier
items.excerpt: How to decipher your PM's AI-generated mockup without losing hours: a practical method for auditing AI-produced prototypes using the sparkle convention as a marker.

items.title: Autodesk releases Maya 2027.3 with new agentic AI features
items.excerpt: Maya 2027.3 gets an updated AI assistant that can edit scenes and a new MCP server for external agents; 3ds Max 2027.3 gets matching agentic workflows plus a DLSS-accelerated Arnold viewport. (Note: movies ran AWN's version 11-19.)

items.title: Research Preview: Pika Enact
items.excerpt: Pika Enact is a research preview of real-time AI filmmaking where creators talk to their cast, rehearse performances and shape scenes as they unfold, directing generated video live rather than prompt-and-wait.

items.title: 퓨저, 문장으로 만드는 맞춤형 편집 도구 공개 (Fuser Tool Node)
items.excerpt: Fuser's 'Tool Node' lets users describe an editing tool in a sentence; the AI designs sliders and switches, writes and tests the tool and places it on the canvas, where it can be chained with other nodes and shared via a team library. (Feature announced 11-13; article 11-18.)

items.title: 에이바 스튜디오, 인기 출시 영상의 컷을 내 제품 화면으로 (Ava Studio Launch Videos)
items.excerpt: Ava Studio's 'Launch Videos' (Claude Code / Codex plugin) analyzes cut order, shot length and camera moves of viral launch videos and rebuilds them with your product screens, logo, colors and type, saved as an editable HyperFrames project.

items.title: Gemini can now be your go-to source for making GIFs
items.excerpt: Google announced Gemini can now create GIFs, using Google's latest video generation model. (Off-list; light AI depth in body.)

items.title: Rhino 9: Patches, SubDs and the AI in the Room
items.excerpt: Rhino 9 brings RhinoAI with AI-assisted commands alongside rebuilt Patch surfacing, Setback fillets, hybrid SubD modeling, enhanced drafting and Grasshopper 2. (Off-list; product/industrial design CAD.)

items.title: A turning point for CAD?
items.excerpt: AI is reshaping CAD, promising smarter tools for product designers while exposing the industry's resistance to rapid change.

items.title: Comsol Conference 2026 highlights: Simulation and AI
items.excerpt: Attendees explored the latest version of the Comsol Multiphysics simulation software and how engineers are using AI within simulation-driven design.

items.title: Can AI Generate Good Designs from Raw User Data?
items.excerpt: In an NN/g study across two design tasks, AI-generated interfaces were better when the model received synthesized research findings and recommendations rather than raw user comments alone.

items.title: When Everything Has Changed, What Do We Do Next?
items.excerpt: A year-end reflection on how AI has upended front-end and web design practice, and what designers and developers should focus on next.

items.title: Google opens Genie 4 world model to developers in Gemini API
items.excerpt: Genie 4 is now in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio for paid-tier developers, a day after Project Genie, at roughly $0.10 per second of streamed interactive world. (Cross-section: games ran DeepMind's Genie 4 post 11-20.)

items.title: Envato's 2nd Annual AI Report Finds Adoption Has Outrun the Rules
items.excerpt: Envato's survey of 1,033 creatives finds 58% use AI daily, 53% have put it on client work without telling the client, and most in-house team creatives have no written AI policy.

items.title: Why 'you don't have to use AI' is the new AI pitch
items.excerpt: Watching Adobe's MAX keynote, the author sees creative-software makers walking a tightrope: being AI-forward while reassuring a hostile creative crowd that AI is optional.

items.title: How Anthropic believes branding will shape its post-IPO future
items.excerpt: Technical superiority alone may not beat competition if users see rival models as interchangeable; Anthropic is betting on brand and design identity as it goes public.

items.title: Artists and creators are leaving Etsy in droves over its new AI policy
items.excerpt: Artistic goodbye messages are flooding social media as makers leave Etsy over its new AI policy.

items.title: Adobe's making design accessible for all – so why am I so anxious?
items.excerpt: Adobe's AI push to democratise design should feel like a utopia; a designer weighs what it means for human creativity and the profession.

items.title: Why Adobe's AI Agents Are Built for Busywork, Not Your Edits
items.excerpt: Glyn Dewis argues AI agents suit repeatable jobs like resizing and renaming, not editing, and tests Claude on a raw sunrise to see where that line falls.
